problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must assign a set of cargo crates to identical transport pallets. The crates are as follows:
* Crate Alpha: mass 69kg
* Crate Beta: mass 49kg
* Crate Gamma: mass 31kg
* Crate Delta: mass 58kg
* Crate Epsilon: mass 36kg
* Crate Zeta: mass 42kg
* Crate Eta: mass 68kg
* Crate Theta: mass 68kg
* Crate Iota: mass 62kg
* Crate Kappa: mass 65kg
* Crate Lambda: mass 30kg
* Crate Mu: mass 44kg
* Crate Nu: mass 40kg
* Crate Xi: mass 30kg
* Crate Omicron: mass 66kg
* Crate Pi: mass 58kg
* Crate Rho: mass 46kg
* Crate Sigma: mass 48kg
* Crate Tau: mass 68kg
* Crate Upsilon: mass 68kg
* Crate Phi: mass 41kg
* Crate Chi: mass 62kg
* Crate Psi: mass 68kg
* Crate Omega: mass 55kg
* Crate A1: mass 50kg
* Crate B1: mass 36kg
* Crate C1: mass 40kg
* Crate D1: mass 37kg
* Crate E1: mass 65kg
* Crate F1: mass 39kg
* Crate G1: mass 60kg
* Crate H1: mass 39kg
* Crate I1: mass 30kg
* Crate J1: mass 68kg
* Crate K1: mass 32kg
* Crate L1: mass 49kg
* Crate M1: mass 43kg
* Crate N1: mass 37kg
* Crate O1: mass 46kg
* Crate P1: mass 46kg

Each pallet has a maximum load capacity of 100 kg. The coordinator must allocate all crates to pallets, using the minimum possible number of pallets. Every crate must be placed on exactly one pallet, and the combined mass on any single pallet must not surpass its capacity limit.
